html:
The Whilkut were an Athabaskan people of the upper Redwood Creek and the Mad River in the hills of northwestern California. Their language was a dialect close to that of the Hupa to the northeast and the Chilula to the north.

They lived in small villages, fished, hunted elk and deer and gathered acorns. Pack trails to the gold mines on the Trinity River crossed their land after 1850, during the Gold Rush. Settlers' militias and the army fought them in the Bald Hills War of the late 1850s and 1860s, and many survivors were moved to the Hoopa Valley reservation. Neighbours: Wiyot and Nongatl.
